Subject: CDN/WAF renewal: evaluation scenarios, cost tradeoffs, and decision log

Hi Laura, Jordan —

We need a short decision log and action plan for the CDN/WAF renewal window coming up in late July. Legal asked for a vendor recommendation by 7/15 so they can prep the PO language; Finance wants to lock committed spend for Q3.

Quick context: our current contract (Cloudflare + managed WAF add-on) expires 8/31. Fastly and Akamai have provided competitive offers. Primary evaluation axes:
- Cost per TB / committed discount tiers
- DDoS / WAF managed rules coverage and false-positive rates
- Latency and cache hit % for our player and static assets
- Contract flexibility (termination, SLA credits, auto-renew clauses)
- Data residency and logging retention for security audits

Can Jordan populate the attached scorecard with the perf numbers you pulled last week, and Laura can you summarize any strategic preference (e.g., single-vendor consolidation vs. poly vendor)? I want a recommendation + top 3 negotiation levers by 7/10 so we can start the vendor calls.

Attachments: none in this message (scorecard to follow).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Partnerships (acting procurement lead)

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the heads up. Attached is Cloudflare Proposal v3 (summary of committed tiers, WAF managed rules, enterprise support SLAs, and DDoS guarantees). Highlights:
- 20% discount on current list if we move to a 12-month committed tier at the 50TB/month level; deeper discounts above 150TB/month.
- WAF: access to Managed Rules, Custom Ruleset support, 90-day false-positive tuning window with a dedicated engineer for migration.
- Logging: 90-day ephemeral logs included; extended log retention is an add-on. We can meet the 12-month retention requirement with the add-on.
- Termination: standard 60-day notice; proposals include a 30-day cure period for SLA disputes.

We included a one-time migration assistance credit (USD 15k) in v3. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with Laura/Jordan to walk the numbers.

Stephanie / Laura —

Attached is the populated scorecard (cdn_waf_scorecard.xlsx). TL;DR summary of my findings after spinning up perf runs and asking for detailed billing: 
- Fastly: best edge cache hit for our dynamic player manifests (avg +3.4% over Cloudflare) but noticeably more expensive at scale once you include WAF managed rules; no explicit DDoS credit in initial bid.
- Akamai: strongest global POP footprint for APAC but license complexity and higher minimums make them a less flexible financial match.
- Cloudflare: lowest combined TCO in our typical traffic bands once you factor in the migration credit and the WAF tuning offer; proposal still has an auto-renew clause that legal will want tightened.

Notes:
1) I added a sensitivity tab modeling cost at ±30% traffic. Cloudflare stays lowest to median in most realistic scenarios.
2) WAF false-positive risk looks higher on Fastly managed rules; they'd charge for additional rule engineering.

Next steps I recommend: 1) push Cloudflare to convert the migration credit to a usage credit (token-based) and remove auto-renew; 2) ask Fastly for an explicit DDoS SLA or credit; 3) ask Akamai to lower the initial commit floor or offer a pilot.

Attachments: cdn_waf_scorecard.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Team —

After reviewing the scorecard, vendor responses, and the negotiation asks: recommendation is to proceed with Cloudflare under the following guardrails. This is my final direction so Legal/Finance can proceed with PO drafting.

Decision: Move forward with Cloudflare (primary), keep Fastly as a fallback for specific player traffic routing (pilot for Q4).

Key reasons:
- TCO: Cloudflare's v3 proposal with the migration credit (if converted to a usage credit) produces the best blended cost across our realistic traffic scenarios.
- Operational risk: Cloudflare's managed WAF and tuning offer reduces lift for Security during migration.
- Timeline: Cloudflare can commit to the ramp schedule that matches our release window.

Required negotiation items before PO:
1) Migration credit must be applied as a usage credit for first 90 days (Ben to confirm in writing).
2) Auto-renew clause removed or set to explicit renewal with 60-day notice and price ceiling.
3) Logging retention: include 12 months for security logs in the base contract or add a capped-rate add-on.
4) SLA credits: include explicit credit schedule for latency and availability misses; legal to draft standard language.

Action owners / next steps:
- Stephanie: confirm with Ben that the migration credit becomes a usage credit and get updated proposal (Ben).
- Jordan: circulate final scorecard snapshot to Finance and Security (shared Drive link included).
- Laura: hand off to Legal/Finance to prepare the PO and DocuSign flow (Finance will reference related_links).

Cc'ing procurement contact so they have the decision on record.

Laura Bennett
VP, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
